title: An In-Context Learning Agent for Formal Theorem-Proving
abstract: We present C OPRA, an in-context learning agent for formal theorem-proving in environments like Lean and Coq. C OPRA uses a general-purpose large language model to propose tactic applications from within a stateful backtracking search, achieving performance comparable to state-of-the-art finetuned approaches.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content:
Imagine you're trying to solve a complex math problem. You can use a large language model to generate potential solutions, but it's hard to know where to start. C OPRA is like a guide that helps the model search for the right solution by proposing tactic applications and using feedback from the proof environment.

This approach is like a conversation between the model and the proof environment, where the model suggests a tactic, the environment responds with feedback, and the model adjusts its next suggestion.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content:
C OPRA uses a large language model to propose tactic applications, which are then executed in the proof environment. The model's output is parsed into a tactic, and the environment's feedback is used to adjust the model's next proposal. This process continues until a proof is found or a timeout is reached.

The model's proposals are guided by a prompt serialization protocol that includes information about the current proof state, the search history, and relevant lemmas retrieved from an external database.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content:
We evaluated C OPRA on the miniF2F benchmark for Lean and a set of Coq proof tasks from the CompCert project. C OPRA outperformed few-shot invocations of GPT-4 and compared favorably to state-of-the-art finetuned approaches.

On miniF2F, C OPRA proved 29.09% of theorems, exceeding the performance of L LEMMA-7b and L LEMMA-34b, and outperforming R E P ROVER in terms of the pass@1 metric.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content:
C OPRA's approach has significant implications for formal theorem-proving. By using a general-purpose large language model, C OPRA can be applied to multiple proof environments without requiring environment-specific training data.

This approach also enables the use of natural-language insights and feedback from the proof environment to guide the search for a proof, making it a more flexible and effective solution than traditional finetuned approaches.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content:
C OPRA's key innovations include its use of a general-purpose large language model, its prompt serialization protocol, and its ability to incorporate feedback from the proof environment and natural-language insights into the search process.

These innovations enable C OPRA to outperform state-of-the-art finetuned approaches and demonstrate the potential of in-context learning for formal theorem-proving.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content:
C OPRA's code and data are available on GitHub, allowing researchers to experiment with the approach and explore its potential applications.

By trying out C OPRA, you can see firsthand how in-context learning can be used to solve complex formal theorem-proving problems and gain insights into the potential of this approach for other applications.
